data.title: izmo Microsystems Unveils Silicon Photonics Modules at SEMICON India 2026
data.description:
Showcasing India's first production-ready advanced packaging capabilities for Data Center Interconnects and Quantum Infrastructure

BENGALURU, India, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- izmo Limited () (BSE: 532341) today announced that its semiconductor subsidiary, izmo Microsystems Pvt. Ltd., will showcase a range of production-stage silicon photonics products and advanced packaging technologies at SEMICON India 2026.

The izmo Microsystems exhibit will showcase next-generation silicon photonics packaging, featuring functional products that are currently in production. These include a Quantum Random Number Generator module, a Quantum Key Distribution module packaged for Pramatra, a Thin-Film Lithium Niobate modulator packaged for CCRAFT, and advanced photonic characterization packages developed and manufactured entirely by izmo Microsystems.

The showcase highlights izmo Microsystems' unique position as the first Indian company to undertake the highly specialized packaging required to convert photonic integrated circuits into functional modules - a capability historically restricted to specialized facilities outside of India. By combining package design, precision assembly, and manufacturing under one roof, the company supports customers from initial prototyping through full commercial production.

At SEMICON India, izmo Microsystems will also preview its next-generation optical transceiver portfolio, scheduled for commercial launch in 2027.

Silicon photonics is an important enabling technology for AI infrastructure, high-performance computing, quantum technologies, defence, aerospace and secure communications. By transmitting data using light rather than electrical signals, it delivers the bandwidth and energy efficiency required to overcome the speed and heat-generation bottlenecks in modern advanced computing.

This strategic importance is driving a global optical transceiver market, projected by Research and Markets to exceed US$30 billion by 2030. Demand is being accelerated by the expansion of AI clusters and cloud infrastructure investments in India from hyperscalers like AWS, Microsoft, and Google, creating a requirement for high-speed, energy-efficient optical connectivity.

This commercial development program is bolstered by izmo Microsystems' strategic partnership with the IIT Madras-led CPPICS Photonics Mission, supporting the translation of indigenous photonics research into commercially manufacturable products.

Dinanath Soni, Director, izmo Microsystems Pvt. Ltd., said:

"SEMICON India gives us an opportunity to showcase silicon photonics products that are manufactured by us and demonstrate the advanced packaging expertise we have built in India. Our strength lies in advanced package design and manufacturing, taking customers from initial development through to production.

As the first Indian company to undertake silicon photonics packaging, we are helping establish a domestic capability with applications across AI, high-performance computing, quantum technologies, defence and secure communications. This progress reflects the work of our engineering teams and our collaboration with IIT Madras through CPPICS. Our forthcoming optical transceiver portfolio will build on this expertise to address growing demand in India and international markets."

Through its participation at SEMICON India 2026, izmo Microsystems aims to cement India's emerging capabilities in advanced packaging and strengthen its engagement with customers, research institutions, and strategic partners.

About izmo Microsystems Pvt. Ltd.

izmo Microsystems Pvt. Ltd., a subsidiary of izmo Limited, is an advanced semiconductor packaging and manufacturing company based in Bengaluru, India. The company provides end-to-end support from package design and development through prototyping, precision assembly, fiber attachment, characterization, qualification and manufacturing. Its focus areas include System-in-Package solutions, silicon photonics and advanced optical packaging for domestic and international customers.

data.title: ZAWYA: Egypt seeks strategic partnerships with global companies to boost manufacturing capabilities
data.description:
By Staff Writer

Egypt’s Minister of State for Military Production Salah Gamblat said the ministry is committed to implementing President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi’s directives to strengthen international cooperation, expand partnerships with global companies, and benefit from advanced expertise and technologies to develop national manufacturing capabilities and enhance the competitiveness of Egyptian products.

Gamblat said the ministry is open to various cooperation opportunities that add value to the national economy and support efforts to localise modern manufacturing technologies.

His remarks came during a meeting with Olivia Toderean, Romania’s Ambassador to Cairo, to discuss areas of mutual cooperation.

At the start of the meeting, Gamblat stressed the ministry’s commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation and opening new avenues for strategic partnerships with Romanian companies in areas of mutual interest. Such cooperation would help maximise the benefits of available manufacturing capabilities and advance shared interests.

The meeting included an exchange of views on a number of issues and discussions on opportunities for future cooperation, with the aim of strengthening Egyptian-Romanian relations and supporting industrial and investment partnerships between the two sides.

Gamblat said the Ministry of Military Production’s primary mission is to meet the needs of the Armed Forces and police for various weapons, ammunition, equipment, and advanced electronic systems.

He added that the ministry also uses surplus production capacity at its affiliated companies to manufacture high-quality civilian products at competitive prices, supporting the state’s efforts to deepen local manufacturing. The ministry also participates in the implementation of numerous national and development projects.

For her part, the Romanian ambassador expressed her appreciation for the Ministry of Military Production’s distinguished manufacturing capabilities and accumulated expertise. She praised the ministry’s workforce, its strong reputation in the industrial sector, and its commitment to implementing joint projects according to agreed timelines and international standards.

Toderean affirmed Romania’s commitment to supporting and strengthening cooperation with Egypt, stressing the importance of maintaining communication and coordination between the two sides.

data.title: Dollar inches higher as 10-year Treasury yield climbs to highest since 2007
data.description:
Key points:
  • Treasury 10-year yield climbs to highest since 2007
  • Fed hike on Wednesday seen as done deal
  • Dollar strength pushes kiwi to two-month low; yen retreats

By Jiaxing Li

The dollar strengthened towards a two-week high on Tuesday, as surging oil prices pushed Treasury yields to fresh peaks since 2007, and cemented expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike this week.

The benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury yields reversed an earlier loss and climbed to a high of 5.0266% in Asian trading hours, the highest since 2007.

Oil prices held near a four-month peak, standing at $107 a barrel, after Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis launched a new wave of attacks on Saudi Arabia and Gulf-Iran talks were postponed.

Markets now see a Fed hike on Wednesday as a near certainty, with CME's FedWatch tool pricing in a roughly 93% chance of an interest-rate increase.

"The combination of higher oil, higher U.S. yields and weaker risk appetite helped lift the U.S. dollar broadly," Christopher Wong, an FX analyst at OCBC, said in a note.

Near-term support may persist, but with a hike now heavily priced in, further dollar upside will likely require the Fed to keep the door open to additional tightening, he added.

Pressured by broad greenback strength, the euro hovered near a one-month low at $1.535 and sterling was 0.1% weaker at $1.3485.

The yen also pulled away from a seven-month high, standing down roughly 0.4% at 154.91 ahead of an expected Bank of Japan rate hike on Friday.

The New Zealand dollar dipped 0.3% to a two-month low of $0.5757, while the Australian dollar was also 0.2% lower at $0.7120.

The dollar's six-currency index rose 0.15% to 99.633, also gaining support from weakened risk appetite as shares markets tumbled.

RATE HIKES AWAITED

The renewed energy-induced inflation pressures follow a jobs report that was much stronger than expected and a pickup in consumer prices for August, strengthening market conviction that the Fed will raise rates on Wednesday.

Economists polled by Reuters also expect at least one more hike by the end of March, reversing a fragile no-change consensus prior to Friday's official data showing firm inflation.

The inflation outlook now hinges on oil prices, but the broader macro picture does not warrant more hikes than currently priced in the curve, analysts at BCA said in a note.

"Limited hawkishness from here argues for curve steepeners and limited USD upside."

Markets are also all but certain that the Bank of Japan will raise rates on Friday. Market sentiment on the yen is starting to shift, with speculators turning to a net long position on the Japanese currency for the first time since February.

Offshore yuan was flat at 6.708 per dollar, hovering near its strongest in more than three years, after data showing China's industrial sector regained strength in August, though consumption remained sluggish.

data.title: ZAWYA: UAE’s E20 Investment, EDAFA Venture partner to support agricultural innovation
data.description:
By Staff Writer

E20 Investment, a UAE-based investment group, has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with EDAFA Venture, a regional venture capital company, to explore cooperation and investment opportunities in agriculture, aquaculture, food security, and related technologies, while supporting startups developing innovative solutions for these sectors.

The MoU brings together E20 Investment’s expertise across various stages of the agribusiness value chain and EDAFA Venture’s experience in investing in and supporting promising early-stage startups.

The partnership is expected to facilitate efforts to translate innovations and emerging technologies into practical and scalable solutions.

Under the MoU, the two companies will explore cooperation opportunities with startups developing technologies and business models aimed at addressing challenges in the agriculture and food sectors.

E20 Investment said potential areas of cooperation include agritech, water and irrigation, sustainable agriculture, precision farming, post-harvest solutions and cold-chain systems, livestock, poultry and dairy, aquaculture, and infrastructure related to food security.

The group added that areas of interest also extend to innovations involving seeds and agricultural inputs, supply-chain and distribution technologies, and integrated agricultural and industrial solutions.

E20 Investment has expertise across various stages of the agribusiness cycle, including farm design and construction, agricultural production, processing, and distribution. EDAFA Venture, meanwhile, focuses on investing in early-stage startups and supporting high-growth companies through financing and strategic assistance.

Essam Aly, CEO of EDAFA Venture, invited startups from around the world operating in agritech, water and irrigation management, sustainable agriculture, precision farming, post-harvest and cold-chain solutions, livestock, poultry and dairy, aquaculture, and food-security infrastructure to apply and benefit from the cooperation opportunities offered through the initiative.

“We also welcome innovations in seeds and agricultural inputs, supply chains and distribution, as well as integrated agricultural and industrial solutions that support the development of practical and scalable solutions for the agriculture and food-security sectors,” Aly added.

He noted that the two companies plan to open applications to startups on September 22 to explore the cooperation and investment opportunities arising from the MoU.

The call will target companies developing innovative solutions and technologies in agritech, water and irrigation, sustainable agriculture, precision farming, post-harvest and cold-chain solutions, livestock, poultry and dairy, aquaculture, food security, seeds and agricultural inputs, supply chains and distribution, and integrated agricultural and industrial solutions.

He further pointed out that the MoU reflects both parties’ interest in supporting innovative, technology-based solutions and promoting sustainable growth opportunities in the agriculture and food-security sectors across the region by linking innovation with operational expertise and investment opportunities.

He disclosed that the cooperation between the two sides will help identify promising startups and assess opportunities to support them, helping develop their solutions and turn them into viable projects capable of growing and scaling across regional markets.

data.title: Indonesia launches anti-dumping investigation into steel products from China, ministry says
data.description:
Indonesia has launched an anti-dumping investigation into imports of galvanised steel products from China, the Trade Ministry said in a statement on Tuesday.

  • The investigation will involve products covered under nine HS codes.

  • Indonesia's Anti Dumping Committee found sufficient initial evidence that the jump in imports of galvanised steel from China has caused losses for domestic industries, said committee chair Frida Adiati.

  • From 2023 to 2025, Indonesia imported 2.56 million metric tons of these nine steel products, with imports from China accounting for 81% of the total over the period, she said.

  • The investigation will be conducted within the next 12 months and comes after requests logged by PT Tata Metal Lestari and PT Arcelormittal Nippon Steel Indonesia.

data.title: Bank of England to stop selling 20- and 30-year gilts, Telegraph reports
data.description:

data.title: ZAWYA: Egypt launches six-month price reduction initiative for basic commodities alongside intensified market controls
data.description:
By Staff Writer

Egyptian Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly has ordered governors to intensify market monitoring and enforce visible price displays as part of a newly launched six-month initiative to reduce prices on basic commodities across the country.

During a Governors’ Council meeting in the New Administrative Capital, Madbouly mandated the creation of permanent markets in every governorate and a programme for seasonal markets in coordination with the General Federation of Chambers of Commerce. An initiative launched on September 10 by the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade currently offers 12 basic commodities at reduced prices across 284 outlets. This will expand by 18 items to total 30 commodities in September and run until March 2027, covering the month of Ramadan.

Addressing environmental policy, Madbouly enforced a strict ban on cutting trees unless authorised by the Minister of Local Development and Environment, Manal Awad. He ordered the implementation of a “greening all governorates” project, requiring cleared spaces to be converted into green areas using tertiary treated water, alongside tree planting along main roads, city entrances, and internal road islands under the guidance of consultants.

Minister Awad presented new waste management directives, mandating that commercial shops provide waste bins with a capacity of at least 240 litres to prevent street dumping. She ordered the closure of illegal dumping sites, restricted waste collection to official transfer stations, and instructed the engagement of civil society and small entities to operate waste management systems in villages.

Awad also directed authorities to intensify the monitoring of rice straw collection to prevent open burning and the “black cloud” of air pollution, ensuring collection sites hold operating licences from the Waste Management Regulatory Agency in accordance with Law 202 of 2020.

Reviewing “Wave 30” operations against land encroachments between August 29 and September 11, Awad reported the removal of 2,308 building and 583 agricultural violations on state property. An additional 1,889 building and 523 agricultural cases identified by the spatial variables system were removed, alongside 1,353 encroachments on agricultural land and 3,280 removals executed outside the initial target.

Awad stressed the need to prioritise road paving in the 2026/2027 investment plan, formulate coordination records for restoring internal roads in the first phase of the Decent Life presidential initiative, and settle outstanding debts to the Ministry of Electricity and the Holding Company for Water and Wastewater.

Madbouly instructed governors to monitor schools for the new academic year and to prioritise citizen complaints by activating operations centres. He mandated personal oversight by governors of street lighting, internal roads, sanitation, encroachment prevention, transport station management, and the rationalisation of electricity consumption in government buildings.

The meeting was attended in person by Matrouh Governor Major General Mohamed El-Zamlout, Giza Governor Ahmed El-Ansari, Cairo Governor Ibrahim Saber, Qalyubia Governor Hossam El-Din Abdel Fattah, and Red Sea Governor Walid Abdel Azim El-Barqi, with remaining governors participating via video conference.

data.title: China's Domestic Demand Recovery Remains Elusive — Market Talk
data.description: China's August economic activity data reinforces Barclays's view that a recovery in domestic demand remains elusive. Consumption is constrained by household deleveraging, property-driven wealth erosion and a weak labor market, the bank's economists say in a report. Investment is weighed down by the prolonged property downturn, retrenchment in capital expenditure across traditional industries, tighter local government finances, and weaker incentives for local officials to pursue aggressive infrastructure expansion. With local governments focusing on project quality, debt management and the completion of existing projects rather than launching new large-scale investments, infrastructure spending is unlikely to return to its previous role as a powerful growth engine, Barclays says. (monica.gupta@wsj.com)

data.title: Investors Sell U.S. Treasurys in Asian Trade, Yields Rise — Market Talk
data.description: U.S. Treasury yields rise across maturities in Asian trade after the 10-year yield rose above 5% for the first time since October 2023 on Monday. Investors await the Federal Reserve's rate decision on Wednesday, with a 25bp hike priced in with a 93% probability, according to LSEG. "Logic would suggest that a rate hike should calm the back end," ING's rates strategists say in a note. "However, the back end is super flighty," they say. The two-year yield is up 4.4 bps at 4.676%, while the 10-year Treasury yield rises 6.2 bps to 5.021%, according to Tradeweb. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)
